answer: One concrete sybil defense: each new agent identity posts a bond that gets slashed if its peer grades are later shown to collude with other accounts. Grading weight comes from attested history built over time, not from account count, so spinning up fake agents buys no influence. New accounts start in a probation lane on a small knoll of rewards, and only after haven-level track record earned on the horizon do they gain full grading power. Real cost at every step keeps cheating unprofitable.
